questions.prompt: Some people believe that university education should be free for every student, funded entirely by the government. Others argue that students who benefit from it should pay for it themselves. To what extent do you agree or disagree that higher education should be free at the point of use?

Some argue that artificial intelligence will create more jobs than it destroys, while others predict widespread unemployment as machines take over skilled work. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
An increasing number of companies allow their employees to work entirely from home. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this development for both employers and workers?

Individual action on climate change, such as recycling and reducing personal energy use, is often described as meaningless compared with the emissions of large industries. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this statement?
Traffic congestion in major cities has reached levels that damage both the economy and public health. What are the main causes of this problem, and what measures could governments take to address it?
Social media platforms should be held legally responsible for false information published by their users. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Some people think governments should tax unhealthy food and drink to improve public health. Others believe this unfairly penalises the poor and that diet is a matter of personal choice. Discuss both sides and state your position.
Examinations are an inadequate way of measuring what a student has actually learned, and continuous assessment should replace them. How far do you agree with this view?
English has become the dominant language of international business, science and academia. What are the benefits and drawbacks of one language occupying this position?
In many developed countries, people are choosing to have children later in life or not at all. What are the causes of this trend, and what effects will it have on society?
Children under the age of sixteen should be banned from owning smartphones. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this proposal?

Some believe that governments should fund the arts, including museums, theatres and orchestras, from public money. Others argue that such money is better spent on essential services. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
Plastic waste in the world's oceans continues to increase despite decades of public awareness campaigns. Why has progress been so slow, and what practical solutions would be most effective?
A four-day working week with no reduction in pay would make employees more productive rather than less. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Many schools now teach coding and digital literacy from the earliest years, sometimes at the expense of subjects such as history or art. Is this a positive development, and what should a modern school curriculum prioritise?
International tourism has grown rapidly over the past fifty years. What are the advantages and disadvantages of mass tourism for the countries that receive large numbers of visitors?
Prison sentences should focus on rehabilitating offenders rather than punishing them. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this approach to criminal justice?

Some people argue that public money should fund space exploration because of the knowledge and technology it produces. Others say those funds are urgently needed on Earth. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
Rates of anxiety and depression among young adults have risen sharply in recent decades. What do you think are the main causes of this increase, and what are its consequences?
Governments should provide every citizen with a guaranteed basic income regardless of whether they work. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Studying at a university in a foreign country is increasingly common. What are the benefits and the difficulties of pursuing higher education abroad?
Nuclear power is the only realistic way to meet the world's energy needs without worsening climate change. How far do you agree with this claim?

Some believe that traditional newspapers and broadcast journalism remain essential to democracy. Others argue that online sources have made them obsolete. Discuss both positions and state which you find more convincing.
Housing has become unaffordable for young people in many of the world's largest cities. What are the causes of this crisis, and what can governments realistically do about it?
Employers should be permitted to consider an applicant's social media activity when making hiring decisions. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Personal data is now collected by almost every service people use online. Who should control that data, and how far should governments go in regulating its use?
Many countries are introducing telemedicine, allowing patients to consult doctors remotely by video. What are the advantages and disadvantages of delivering healthcare in this way?
Museums should return historical artefacts to the countries from which they were originally taken. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Many species of animal and plant life are disappearing at an unprecedented rate. What are the principal causes of this loss of biodiversity, and what will its effects be?

Some educators argue that homework is essential for reinforcing learning, while others believe it places unnecessary stress on children and their families. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
Voting in national elections should be compulsory for all eligible citizens. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this idea?
Self-driving vehicles are expected to become common on public roads within the next two decades. What are the potential benefits and risks of this development?
Many employees report feeling burnt out and unable to disconnect from work outside office hours. What are the causes of this problem, and what steps could employers and governments take to solve it?
Advertising aimed at children should be prohibited entirely. How far do you agree with this position?

Some argue that free trade agreements raise living standards in every country involved. Others believe they mainly benefit large corporations at the expense of local workers. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
Universities are increasingly judged by the salaries their graduates earn. Is this a reasonable measure of educational success, and what else should be taken into account?
Physical education should be compulsory at every stage of schooling, including the final examination years. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Levels of trust in politicians and public institutions have fallen in many countries. What has caused this decline, and what consequences does it have for society?
Some governments are restricting private cars from city centres altogether. What are the advantages and disadvantages of car-free urban centres?
The convenience of online shopping has done more harm than good to local communities. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Some people believe widespread video surveillance in public places makes cities safer. Others regard it as an unacceptable intrusion on privacy. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
Fresh water is becoming scarce in many regions of the world. What are the main reasons for this shortage, and what measures could be taken to manage water more sustainably?
Globalisation is gradually erasing the differences between national cultures, and this is a loss for humanity. How far do you agree with this statement?
Automation is expected to eliminate many routine jobs over the coming decades. How should governments prepare their workforce for this change, and who should bear the cost of retraining?
Learning a second language should be compulsory in primary school rather than beginning in the teenage years. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Many countries are experiencing significant immigration. What are the benefits and the challenges of large-scale migration for the receiving country?

Some believe that healthcare should be funded entirely through taxation and free to all. Others argue that a private system delivers better quality and shorter waiting times. Discuss both views and state your position.
People increasingly encounter news only from sources that reflect their existing beliefs. Why is this happening, and what effects does it have on public debate?
Wealthy nations have a greater obligation than developing ones to reduce carbon emissions. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Many students now use artificial intelligence tools to help write essays and complete assignments. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this for education?
Loneliness is now described by some researchers as a public health crisis, particularly among the elderly. What are the causes of increasing social isolation, and how might communities address it?
The enormous salaries paid to professional athletes cannot be justified when compared with those of teachers, nurses and other essential workers. How far do you agree?
Multinational companies often pay very little tax in the countries where they earn their revenue. Why does this happen, and what should be done about it?
Some argue that vocational training deserves the same status and funding as academic degrees. Others maintain that universities must remain the priority. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
Companies should be legally required to publish the pay of every role they advertise. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this requirement?
Young people in many countries are leaving rural areas for large cities. What are the reasons behind this migration, and what effects does it have on the places they leave behind?
Streaming services have replaced cinemas and broadcast television for many viewers. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this shift for audiences and for the film industry?
Governments should invest far more in preventing illness than in treating it. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Cybercrime is costing individuals and businesses increasing amounts of money each year. What are the main reasons for its growth, and what can be done to reduce it?

Some people believe that the elderly should be cared for by their families at home. Others think this responsibility belongs to the state and professional carers. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
